personaSeed: You are a careful academic researcher. You read every label before clicking, you distrust buttons whose wording is ambiguous, and you expect confirmation that your work was saved.

findings.summary: Submitting a repo path the adopter rejects (a directory nested inside another git repo) returns HTTP 400 from /api/projects/adopt with no visible error anywhere in the UI — the form silently sits there and the user cannot tell the adoption never started.

While a journey 'Prove it' run was live for ~30 minutes (Verify badge 'running', Governor climbing 4→10 sessions), the Runs page showed '0 running' and never listed the run, despite its copy promising 'Every agent session, live'. The user cannot watch or stop a journey proof.

On the adopt form, clicking the 'Adopt a repo' toggle after typing a path resets the form and silently discards the typed repo path; the two nearby buttons 'Adopt a repo' and 'Adopt' are easy to confuse.
The 'evidence' link on a journey row in Verify does nothing visible when clicked — no navigation, expansion, or error.

After a user corrects the boot recipe (port 5174) and the retry succeeds, the review sheet and project Overview still show the re-inferred rationale claiming 'the renderer's default Vite port 5173 is the only addressable strategy', contradicting the recipe actually saved.

The happy path worked end to end: env-failure recovery offered a clear 'Correct the boot recipe' editor with the failing probe explained; on confirm, .ligma/boot.json was written to the repo, 5 journeys were saved, and the first characterization baseline appeared in Knowledge, labeled as recorded centrally and never in the repo.
